CHAPTER III · THE CHURCH IN ACTS

And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.
He is named fifth among the Eleven in the upper room (Acts 1:13). Acts never names the apostle again.

VIEWS, WITH WHO HOLDS THEM · THIS PAGE
Which Philip lived and was buried at Hierapolis?
Polycrates of Ephesus (about 190); Clement of Alexandria (about 200)
Polycrates calls him “Philip, one of the twelve apostles”, with daughters. Clement names Philip with Peter among the married apostles.
The household of Philip the evangelist

Proclus speaks of “four prophetesses, the daughters of Philip” at Hierapolis. Acts gives Philip the evangelist “four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy” (Acts 21:8–9). Eusebius sets the two reports side by side without comment.
